bindings.label: Patient presented with stridor, increased work of breathing, and supplemental oxygen requirement

Patient was transferred from an outside hospital to the ED after falling with an e-cigarette in his mouth several hours earlier; he did not remember the exact cause of the fall and believed he may have lost consciousness.
Physical examination in the ED showed diffuse supraglottic edema most severe in the epiglottis, arytenoids, and aryepiglottic folds, which obstructed the view of the true vocal cords.
CT confirms glottic and supraglottic swelling without fractures
Direct laryngoscopy reveals diffuse edema with mucosal sloughing most severe in the epiglottis
Esophageal scar and antral ulceration are identified on additional evaluation
Inflammatory markers and culture results are unavailable, so infectious supraglottitis cannot be fully excluded
